likely: Group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) — when Centor score is high
possible: Fusobacterium necrophorum (consider in older adolescents/young adults with severe symptoms)
pathogens.why: Most pharyngitis is viral. Group A Streptococcus becomes a relevant consideration only with sufficient Centor criteria, and testing (rapid antigen detection or culture) should confirm before treating to avoid unnecessary antibiotic exposure.

investigations.test: Rapid antigen detection test (RADT) or throat culture
investigations.why: Confirms or excludes Group A Streptococcus before committing to antibiotics, directly preventing unnecessary use in viral pharyngitis.
